An update from my attempts to troubleshoot that. I only get this error if I have already run the compileNimble previously in the R session. If it is a new R session, my code runs just fine. Not sure if this helps explain anything, but I'd love to understand still what is going on here!

Thanks,
Annie

On Wednesday, November 1, 2023 at 12:29:46 PM UTC-4 Annie Shapiro wrote:
Hi again, 

I was previously able to get my code to run, but I'm now getting the following error and I don't believe I've changed anything. I've attached sample data if that's helpful. I have the following code, and get an error that I need to define the random function for my user-defined distribution. After reading the user manual, it doesn't appear that I should need it. Furthermore, this code previously ran without issue. Any thoughts as to what is happening here? 

Thanks!
Annie

Here is my code:
#====================================================================
# functions
#====================================================================

f_vec <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0)){
   
    # #Phl:
    k <- 6.06
    r <- 2.94

    tmp_vec <- rep(NA, x)
   
    for (i in 1:x) {
      tmp_vec[i] <- pgamma(x-(i-1), k, rate = r) - pgamma(x-i, k, rate = r)
    }
   
    return(tmp_vec)
    returnType(double(1))
  })

# code penalty as prior
dpen <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1),
                 theta = double(0), L = double(0),
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    logProb <- -(theta/2)*sum((log(x[1:(L-2)]) - 2*log(x[2:(L-1)]) + log(x[3:L]))^2)
    if(log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb))
  })
#====================================================================
# set up MCMC
#====================================================================
modelCode <- nimbleCode({
 
  for (i in 1:L){
    #get mu
    mu[i] <- sum(f_vec(i)*lambda[1:i])
   
    #likelihood
    x[i] ~ dpois(mu[i])}
 
  #priors
  lambda[1:L] ~ dpen(theta = theta, L = L)
  # k ~ T(dnorm(6.06, .1), 0, )
  # r ~ T(dnorm(2.94, .05), 0, )
 
  #hyperprior
  theta ~ dunif(1, 100)
})



modelConsts <- list(L = nrow(dat))

modelData <- list(x = dat$Notifications)

# initsList <- list(lambda = abs(rnorm(nrow(dat), mean(dat$Notifications), sd(dat$Notifications))))


model <- nimbleModel(modelCode, data = modelData,  constants = modelConsts) #inits = initsList,
#====================================================================
# Compile and run model
#====================================================================

# compile into nimble
Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)

And here is the error I get when compiling my model: 
Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'rpen' is not available or its output type is unknown. This occurred for: eigenBlock(model_lambda,1:29) <<- rpen(=1,theta=model_theta[1],L=29) This was part of the call: { eigenBlock(model_lambda,1:29) <<- rpen(=1,theta=model_theta[1],L=29) }

Hi Annie,
I replaced your read_excel line with reading the file you provided previously (which looked already filtered and selected).
By "clear the environment", I tried "rm(list = ls())".
I was able to reproduce the problem. Thanks for this report. I will file a GitHub issue (with a minimal reproducible version of the problem) and it will take some investigation, especially if it is, as you said, a new problem.
If you want a workaround so you can use your workflow and not encounter this, you can do
deregisterDistributions("dpen")
when you are clearing the environment.
HTH
Perry
